answer: Verify each agent by post. The agent registers a street address, say a house on River Terrace. The network mails a letter carrying a one-time code printed in UV pigment ink. The agent photographs the letter under a UV lamp and submits the code. A photocopy fails because the pigment only glows under UV light. One address can hold one identity, so an attacker who wants 10,000 fake agents must rent 10,000 real mailboxes at about $10 each per month, or $100,000 a month, plus $2 postage per letter. When a mailbox lapses, its identity dies with it.
